NIMBY means "Not In My Back Yard". It's the tendency of land owners, typically those on the urbanized coast, to be strongly opposed to local new power plants, despite the fact that closer generation is more effective for satisfying reactive power demands used by heavy inductive loads like air conditioners.

If you can't build plants close, then you need high voltage transmission lines and local capacitor banks. Capacitor banks are needed because only real power (which serves resistive load) can be transmitted over long distances. Reactive power (which is consumed by inductive load) is subject to the same physical constraints on transmission as direct current (about 2 miles on copper). However, with a capacitor bank (typical co-located at the nearest transformer station), inductive load can be made to LOOK (to the rest of the gird) like resistive load, by creating a local current loop. However, capacitors like to go boom.
